AgentKey is a gateway to live external data: web search, page scraping, social platforms, finance, crypto, e-commerce and company data. It does not expose one tool per provider. Instead it exposes a small set of meta tools, and you discover the real capability at runtime.

## The three-step flow

1. `find_tools` — describe the data you need in plain language and get back the matching tools. The catalog changes over time, so ALWAYS start here. Never guess or hardcode a tool name.

skills.body:
# DubLab

DubLab dubs videos into 90+ languages with voice cloning. There is no MCP server;
call its REST API with curl.

- Base URL: `https://dublab.app/api/v2`
- Auth header: `apikey: $DUBLAB_API_KEY` (`Authorization: Bearer` is also accepted)
- The key is available in the environment as `DUBLAB_API_KEY`. Never print it.
- Fields are snake_case. Errors return `{"error":"message"}` with 400/401/402/404/413/502/500.

## 1. Check credits and languages
```bash
curl -sS https://dublab.app/api/v2/me -H "apikey: $DUBLAB_API_KEY"
```
`seconds` is the credit balance (1 credit = 1 second of output). Check it before dubbing
a long video; a 402 means not enough credits.

Language codes come from `GET https://dublab.app/api/langs` (public, no auth): use the
`code` field as `dest_lang` / `source_lang`.

## 2. Create a dub
Either upload a local file (multipart, up to 1 GB) or pass a public URL.
```bash
curl -sS --max-time 900 -X POST https://dublab.app/api/v2/dubs \
  -H "apikey: $DUBLAB_API_KEY" \
  -F source_lang=en -F dest_lang=fr \
  -F "file=@video.mp4;type=video/mp4"
```
```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://dublab.app/api/v2/dubs \
  -H "apikey: $DUBLAB_API_KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"source_url":"https://example.com/video.mp4","dest_lang":"fr"}'
```
Parameters: `dest_lang` (required), `source_lang` (default `auto`), `name`, `duration`,
`is_studio_quality` (true = 2x credits). Returns the dub `id`.

**One target language per call**: dubbing into 3 languages means 3 POSTs.

## 3. Poll until done
```bash
curl -sS https://dublab.app/api/v2/dubs/<id> -H "apikey: $DUBLAB_API_KEY"
```
`external_status_id`: 1 uploading, 2 in queue, 3 processing, 4 failed, 5 completed.
Poll every ~30s and follow `progress_percentage`. On 4, read `external_error_message`.

## 4. Collect the outputs
`outputs` stays empty until status 5, then holds `translated_mp4`, `translated_mp3` and
`translated_subtitle`, each with a `url` and a `download_url`. Those links are presigned
and expire after roughly 1 hour, so download them right away or re-fetch the dub to get
fresh ones.

`GET /api/v2/dubs?page=1&page_size=20` lists past dubs, newest first.

## Rules
- Dubbing costs credits and takes minutes: confirm the video and the target languages
  with the user before creating a dub, and never re-create a job just to retry a poll.
- Set generous timeouts on uploads (`--max-time 900`); a slow upload is not a failure.

- `search_calls` - flexible search with filters (date range, workspace, participants).

- `get_trackers` - the workspace's configured keyword trackers (competitors, objections, pricing).

An older install may carry `HF_API_KEY_ID` and `HF_API_KEY_SECRET` instead: join them as `${HF_API_KEY_ID}:${HF_API_KEY_SECRET}`.

## REST API (API key)

Base URL `https://api.higgsfield.ai`, header `Authorization: Key ${HF_KEY}`.

1. Pick a model from https://docs.higgsfield.ai/docs/models/image-generation.md or https://docs.higgsfield.ai/docs/models/video-generation.md. Each model page (`https://docs.higgsfield.ai/docs/models/<model>/<workflow>.md`) gives the Endpoint ID and the exact request schema. Never guess fields.
2. Submit:
```
curl -sS -X POST "https://api.higgsfield.ai/<endpoint-id>" \
  -H "Authorization: Key ${HF_KEY}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prompt":"..."}'
```
It returns `request_id`, `status_url` and `cancel_url`. Use those URLs, do not build them by hand.
3. Poll `status_url` with the same header (start at 2 s, back off to 10 s) until the status is `completed`, `failed`, `nsfw` or `canceled`. A completed request carries `images[].url`, `video.url` or `audio.url`; outputs stay available for at least 7 days, download them if they must last longer.
4. Local input file: `POST https://api.higgsfield.ai/files/generate-upload-url` with `{"content_type":"image/png"}`, PUT the file to `upload_url` with every header in `upload_headers` (never send the Higgsfield credentials there), then pass `public_url` as `image_url` / `video_url` / `audio_url`.
5. Never repeat a generation POST after an ambiguous timeout: submissions have no idempotency key and it would bill twice. Cancel with `POST cancel_url` while the request is still queued.

Errors: 401 bad credentials, 403 insufficient API balance (tell the user to top up in open.higgsfield.ai), 422 body does not match the schema (re-read the model page), 423 / 503 model temporarily unavailable. Failed and nsfw requests are not charged.

## Generating well

- Write prompts as a shot description: subject, action, setting, lighting, lens and mood. Vague prompts produce generic results.
- Video generation is asynchronous and slow. Start the job, then poll for its status instead of assuming the first response contains the final asset.
- Return the resulting asset URL to the user, and reuse the same character or seed across calls when a series must stay visually consistent.

# Instagram

You act as the connected Instagram business or creator account. Call `instagram_INSTAGRAM_GET_USER_INFO` with `ig_user_id: "me"` first: most tools need the numeric account id it returns as `ig_user_id`.

## Publishing

Publishing always takes two steps: create a container, then publish it.

1. Create the container:
   - Single photo: `instagram_INSTAGRAM_POST_IG_USER_MEDIA` with `image_url` (a public JPEG URL).
   - Reel: same tool with `media_type: "REELS"` and `video_url` (a public MP4 URL).
   - Story: same tool with `media_type: "STORIES"` and an image or video URL.
   - Carousel (2 to 10 items): `instagram_INSTAGRAM_CREATE_CAROUSEL_CONTAINER` with `child_image_urls` / `child_video_urls` and the caption.
2. Publish with `instagram_INSTAGRAM_POST_IG_USER_MEDIA_PUBLISH`, passing the container id as `creation_id`. It waits for videos to finish processing.

Media must be reachable at a public URL Meta can fetch. Containers expire within 24 hours, so publish right after creating. Instagram caps posts per 24 hours: check `instagram_INSTAGRAM_GET_IG_USER_CONTENT_PUBLISHING_LIMIT` before publishing several in a row. Posts cannot be scheduled nor edited after publishing, apart from turning comments on or off with `instagram_INSTAGRAM_SET_MEDIA_COMMENT_ENABLED`.

Always show the user the exact media and caption and wait for approval before publishing.

## Reading and analytics

`instagram_INSTAGRAM_GET_IG_USER_MEDIA` lists the published posts, `instagram_INSTAGRAM_GET_IG_MEDIA` reads one (use the numeric media id, not the shortcode from the post URL), `instagram_INSTAGRAM_GET_IG_MEDIA_CHILDREN` lists the items of a carousel. `instagram_INSTAGRAM_GET_IG_USER_STORIES` lists the active stories, `instagram_INSTAGRAM_GET_IG_USER_TAGS` the posts the account is tagged in.

`instagram_INSTAGRAM_GET_USER_INSIGHTS` returns account metrics (reach, views, followers), `instagram_INSTAGRAM_GET_IG_MEDIA_INSIGHTS` the metrics of one post (views, reach, likes, comments, saved, shares). Insights can come back empty on small accounts or very recent posts: say so instead of retrying.

## Comments

Read with `instagram_INSTAGRAM_GET_IG_MEDIA_COMMENTS` and `instagram_INSTAGRAM_GET_IG_COMMENT_REPLIES`. Reply with `instagram_INSTAGRAM_POST_IG_COMMENT_REPLIES`, comment on a post with `instagram_INSTAGRAM_POST_IG_MEDIA_COMMENTS`, answer a mention with `instagram_INSTAGRAM_POST_IG_USER_MENTIONS`. Draft replies for the user's approval unless they asked you to answer on your own. Use `instagram_INSTAGRAM_DELETE_COMMENT` only when the user asks for a deletion.

## Direct messages

`instagram_INSTAGRAM_LIST_ALL_CONVERSATIONS` (with `platform: "instagram"`) lists the threads, `instagram_INSTAGRAM_LIST_ALL_MESSAGES` reads one. Reply with `instagram_INSTAGRAM_SEND_TEXT_MESSAGE` or `instagram_INSTAGRAM_SEND_IMAGE`, using the recipient id from the conversation, never a username. You can only answer someone who wrote first, within Instagram's messaging window: if the send fails with error subcode 2534022, tell the user and do not retry. Mark a thread read with `instagram_INSTAGRAM_MARK_SEEN`. Show the user every DM before sending unless they asked you to answer on your own.

## Not available

Personal Instagram accounts, other people's profiles and follower lists, starting a new DM thread, scheduling, editing a published caption, and ads are out of reach. Ads live in the Meta Ads app.

skills.body:
# Klubizz The connection carries one Klub: every tool acts on it and on no other. Call `me` first to see which Klub, which plan and which rate limit you have. ## The shape of a Klub - A **space** holds posts or content. Its `accessType` is one of `free`, `tier`, `one_time`, `free_price`, `staff`. - A **tier** is an offer (subscription, one-off, lifetime, instalments) carrying one or more prices. - Spaces and space groups are born as drafts. Publishing is a second call with `isDraft: false`. ## Rules the API enforces - **A member holds one tier at a time.** `tier_grant` replaces the tier they had, it never adds to it. Selling two things at once needs a bundle tier. - **Post bodies are HTML.** Newlines collapse at render, so write `

`, `

`, `` — never plain text with `\n`. - **There is no `post_update`.** Fixing a post means `post_create` then `post_delete`, and the delete is irreversible: recreate first, delete second. - **`tier_update` replaces the whole offer.** Send `prices` back every time or they are wiped. A tier's type is immutable after creation. - A paid tier cannot move to `visibility: invite`. # Lightreel

Lightreel answers marketing research questions over a database of 150,000+ TikTok
and Instagram UGC videos. There is no MCP server; call its REST API with curl.

- Base URL: `https://api.lightreel.ai`
- Auth header: `Authorization: Bearer $LIGHTREEL_API_KEY`
- The key is available in the environment as `LIGHTREEL_API_KEY`. Never print it.

## Ask a question
```bash
curl -sS --max-time 600 -X POST https://api.lightreel.ai/v1/chat \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $LIGHTREEL_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"question":"find me the top fitness hooks this week"}'
```
Returns `{ "conversationId": "...", "answer": "..." }`. Pass `conversation_id` to
continue an existing thread.

## Structured output
Add `response_fields` (max 5 fields, types `"string"` or `"array"` only) to get JSON
inside `answer` instead of prose. Put the expected content AND the supporting evidence
you want in each description. For several attributes about the same items, use several
arrays and say in the descriptions that they are index-aligned.
```bash
-d '{
  "question": "Find fitness creators who post workout vlogs and are open to brand deals",
  "response_fields": {
    "handles":      { "type": "array", "description": "One creator handle per entry" },
    "descriptions": { "type": "array", "description": "What the creator posts, index-aligned with handles" },
    "top_videos":   { "type": "array", "description": "Best performing video from the last 2 weeks, index-aligned with handles" }
  }
}'
```

## Transcripts
- `GET /v1/chat/:id` - one past conversation.
- `GET /v1/chats` - the latest 50 API chats.

## Rules
- Requests can take **several minutes**. Always set a generous timeout (`--max-time 600`);
  a timeout is not a failure of the query.
- The more context in the question (product, audience, platform, timeframe), the better
  the answer. Be specific rather than terse.
- Errors return a non-2xx with `{"error":{"message":…,"type":…}}`; `authentication_error`
  means the key is missing or invalid.
- API calls draw from the account's normal usage quota, so avoid redundant repeat queries.

Use the notion tools to search, read and update pages and databases. Always confirm before creating or overwriting content.

## What the connection mode changes

**Sign in with Notion** (Notion's hosted MCP server): the agent inherits the signed-in user's own Notion permissions and gets the full toolset, including comments and database views. - Database views cannot be listed, created or edited at all. Notion's public REST API has no view endpoints.

In both cases, do not retry: tell the user that this needs the "Sign in with Notion" connection mode, and that they can switch it from the connector panel.

# Typeform

Use the typeform_* tools to work inside the user's Typeform account.

Resolve ids before anything else. typeform_list_forms returns each form's id, title, public state and public URL; typeform_list_workspaces gives the workspace ids used when creating a form. Never guess an id.

typeform_upsert_webhook posts every new submission to a URL. The tag is the webhook name, so reusing a tag updates that webhook instead of adding another one.

skills.body:
# ZipRecruiter Job Search

The ZipRecruiter MCP server exposes a single read-only tool, `search_jobs`, for finding live job listings in the United States and Canada.

## search_jobs
Search parameters (all optional unless noted):
- `job_role`: specific role, e.g. `software engineer`. Omit for broad searches.
- `skills`: array of relevant skills, e.g. `["SQL"]`.
- `location`: concrete city, state, zip, or address (e.g. `Montreal, Quebec`). Ask the user for a location before searching unless they want remote jobs; without a location the search defaults to a US-wide search and warns.
- `radius_miles`: search radius from the location.
- `country_admin_code`: ISO-3166-1 alpha-2 country code, only when a concrete location makes the country known.
- `max_posted_minutes_ago`: minimum 1440 (jobs posted within N minutes).
- `salary_min` / `salary_max`: annual salary filters (0–300000).
- `location_types`: PHYSICAL, REMOTE, HYBRID.
- `employment_types`: FULL_TIME, PART_TIME, CONTRACT, CONTRACT_TO_HIRE, TEMPORARY, AS_NEEDED, INTERNSHIP, OTHER.
- `seniority_classes`: NO_EXPERIENCE, JUNIOR, MID, SENIOR.
- `offset`: pagination offset.

## Tips
- Only provide fields the user explicitly stated.
- To search multiple distinct roles, call the tool once per role for cleaner results.
- Results include a `job_redirect_url` that opens the listing on ZipRecruiter to view details or apply.
